title: Harvard researchers find AI coding agents shifted the bottleneck to code review
excerpt: Editor’s Note: Engineers at firms that adopted AI coding agents added about 30 percent more code, yet finished work did not measurably rise and getting code through review took 49 percent longer, according to a working paper by Harvard Ph.D. candidates Fiona Chen and James Stratton covering 718 firms. The paper, a job-market paper with no indication of completed peer review, measures what happens at the human checkpoint once drafting speeds up. rejectedSummary: A working paper by Harvard Ph.D. candidates Fiona Chen and James Stratton, covering 718 firms, found engineers at firms that adopted AI coding agents added about 30 percent more code. Finished work did not measurably rise, and getting code through review took 49 percent longer. The paper is a job-market paper with no indication of completed peer review.
